automorphism_and_C4_classification.verdict: The intrinsic two-foliation bounds the full automorphism group of the product Y by its two block-preserving G60 leaf restrictions. The explicit normalizer quotient attains that bound.  The center and every foliation-exchanging order-four square root are then classified abstractly; the successful unordered tau pair selects one C4 branch while factor reversal changes only its orientation.

formal_argument: An automorphism fixing a vertex and both intrinsic colors fixes its two root leaves setwise.
Each root-leaf restriction lies in the order-four point stabilizer of C_AutG60(b), giving an upper bound 4 x 4.
If both restrictions are identity, complete 30 x 30 leaf incidence fixes every leaf setwise.
The all-block kernel on each leaf is {identity,b}; each two-vertex cell forces the two incident leaf bits equal.
The K30,30 agreement graph is connected, so all 60 bits are equal; a fixed root leaf forces the common bit zero.

automorphism_completeness_closure.verdict: The normalizer quotient acts faithfully with prequotient kernel exactly diag<b>.  Its sixteen color-preserving anchor stabilizer elements realize all sixteen distinct pairs of four native root-leaf restrictions, saturating the intrinsic upper bound.  The complete leaf-cell agreement graph closes the restriction injectivity lemma. Delta and the two C4 conjugacy branches are intrinsic; source tau selects the a branch and one labeled embedded subgroup, while bare Y selects neither a unique conjugate nor K over K^-1.

clauses: Aut(Y) is ((C_Aut(G60)(b) x C_Aut(G60)(b)) rtimes C2_swap) / <diag(b)>, of order 57600, with 28800 elements of each factor parity.
Z(Aut(Y)) is {identity,E,Delta,E_Delta}, isomorphic to V4; its three nonidentity regular 900-vertex quotients are pairwise nonisomorphic.
Delta is the unique nonidentity central element admitting a factor-exchanging square root, so Delta and X=Y/<Delta> are intrinsic to the bare graph.

The 240 oriented order-four roots of Delta form 120 C4 subgroups in two Aut(Y)-classes of 60, with terminal quotients B_a and B_ab isomorphic to B_b, respectively; those two terminal types are nonisomorphic.
In labeled product coordinates tau=(ab,b) defines K and one embedded C4; reversing tau gives K^-1 and the same subgroup. Bare Y can select neither one conjugate nor one orientation.
